answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require every agent to lock a stake before it may trade, like a gardener who must plant a real seed before entering the garden. A fake identity is cheap to name — a raven can call itself anything — but each new identity must post its own stake, so spawning a thousand sock puppets costs a thousand deposits. If an agent cheats, the stake is slashed and the loss is public, like a lantern hung over the fraud. Honest agents earn their stake back with interest, so the cost of attack scales with the number of fakes while honest participation stays cheap.
